handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

title: M3 built, tested twice. Blind test confirmed real (+0.3% total but with significant error cancellation). Next: improve line-item accuracy.
status: M3 WORKING. Two test runs complete. Blind test infrastructure solid. Ready to improve individual line-item reasoning.

first_thing_next_session: Dive into M3 line-item accuracy. test_1_result.description: NOT a real blind test. Woodman data was still in the knowledge pack unit_price_distributions (unit prices AND quantities per-observation). Claude explicitly used Woodman actuals mid-reasoning, e.g. 'I'll round to $4,800 to match what Woodman actually spent'.
test_1_result.verdict: Directionally valid but contaminated. Disregard as a blind accuracy test.

test_2_result.description: Real blind test. holdout_woodman knowledge pack used. Thinking file confirmed zero Woodman data references — all pricing from Killdeer, Boyds, Painted Rock, Mountainside, Solara.
test_2_result.verdict: Real blind test. Total looks excellent but is misleading — ~$65k of overestimates cancelled ~$60k of underestimates. Error cancellation, not precision.

gemini_extraction.note: road_LF actual is 927.65 LF (Gemini read STA 10+00 to 20+00 = 1,000 LF). ROW width 68 ft is the true ROW; case library ROW_SF (81,757) uses wider corridor including 10' easements on each side.

blind_test_error_analysis.summary: The +0.3% total masks ~$65k overestimates cancelling ~$60k underestimates. Nolan wants to attack this — keep the overall score but improve underneath accuracy.

large_overestimates.root_cause: Formula (22 × 0.23 = 5.06 → 5 EA) fired correctly by the rules. But Woodman uses swale-based drainage — swale jobs suppress drywells. Without Woodman's actual in the pack, nothing flagged this. The system prompt says 'floor at 2 for small jobs' but 22 lots is not small, so the rule didn't trigger.
Purely an LS estimation problem. No formula. Claude doubled the typical median. This item is highly variable and hard to estimate without topography data.
No formula — analog scaling. Killdeer/Boyds both have 2 EA. Woodman is an unusually small hydrant count (1 EA) for 22 lots. Hard to fix without a formula.

large_overestimates.item: Scope creep items (Signs/Striping, Ped Ramps, Traffic Control)
large_overestimates.actual: $0 (not in Terra scope — in exclusions list)
large_overestimates.root_cause: Claude adds these from analogs that include them. Terra Underground's standard exclusions list omits these. Need to add an explicit exclusion list to the system prompt.
Without Woodman's $15,200 LS in the pack, Claude averaged Killdeer/Painted Rock and came in high.

large_underestimates.root_cause: Woodman held out. With only 1-2 remaining ballast observations (Lone Fir $10.50, Mountainside $12.22), Claude estimated $11.50/SY median. Woodman's $17.40 was the only current-market 12" ballast data point. Ballast is thin data — this is a real fragility.

Claude checked whether analogs included this as a separate line item and concluded Killdeer/Boyds/Painted Rock didn't, so excluded it. But Woodman does have it. This is a Gemini extraction gap — the typical section or scope notes should flag driveway approaches.
Woodman's $3,300/EA removed. Most recent remaining observation was Solara $2,900. The strong recency-weighting rule fired and pushed the price down.
Formula: round(570 LF / 250) = 2. But Claude underestimated sewer main LF (570 vs actual 743 LF). The sewer LF estimate drove the manhole count error.

next_session_goal.nolans_words: Dive into the reasoning behind the number to see if I can keep a good overall score but with an improved underneath score.
next_session_goal.translation: Maintain overall ±5-10% accuracy but reduce the error cancellation — get individual line items closer so the estimate is right for the right reasons, not because overestimates and underestimates happen to cancel.

suggested_attack_order.fix: Add Terra Underground standard exclusions to system prompt
suggested_attack_order.impact: -$33,660 of phantom scope creep removed. These are in Terra's standard exclusions list on every proposal.

suggested_attack_order.fix: Add swale detection to drywell logic
suggested_attack_order.detail: Gemini already extracts scope_notes. If scope_notes mentions 'swale' or 'infiltration', suppress the drywell formula and use analog scaling instead. Woodman scope_notes: 'infiltration grassy swales with drywells (Sheet C-11/C-14)'. The word 'swales' should floor drywells at 2.

Add to Gemini prompt: extract whether driveway approaches are a separate scope item. Also add to Claude system prompt: 'CONCRETE APPROACH (driveway aprons) — include as a line item for subdivision road jobs at approx lot_count × 100 SF × $9.30/SF unless analogs consistently omit it'.

Only 1-2 observations without Woodman. Consider flagging in Claude prompt when KP ballast_per_SY has N<3 — use the highest observed price rather than the median when data is thin. Or cross-check against the typical section spec thickness to catch unusually thick sections.
suggested_attack_order.impact: -$22,904 ballast underestimate is a real fragility

suggested_attack_order.detail: Sewer main LF is currently estimated by ROW_SF analog scaling. The estimate came in at 570 LF vs actual 743 LF (23% low). Consider adding a second formula check: if typical section shows deep sewer (7-11'), the main likely follows the road closely at ~0.75-0.80× road_LF. Could also detect sewer depth from Gemini (the Woodman quantity sheet notes '7-11' depth').

open_questions: Is Terra's standard exclusions list written down anywhere (proposal template, exclusions_text field in case library)? If so, extract it and hardcode into the M3 system prompt. Currently each proposal has exclusions_text but it's not being fed to the Claude prompt.

The Gemini road_LF extraction reads STA 10+00 to 20+00 = 1,000 LF. The true road_LF is 927.65 LF (hand-read from plan stationing). The 1,000 LF is what Gemini sees from the sheet numbers — this 8% error propagates through the whole estimate. Worth noting for future validation.
Ballast unit price data is thin (N=1 without Woodman). Need more jobs in the case library before this is stable. Flag in prompt when N<3.

Fire hydrant count has no reliable formula and is consistently wrong (1 vs 2 predicted). The range in the case library is 1-9 (outlier: Settlement Mountain at 9). May need Gemini to try to count hydrant symbols from the utility plan sheet.
